Porsche Unveils New and Discreet Dashcam Packing High-Res Recording With HDR
9 photos
Photo: Porsche
In case you didn't know, among the endless accessories you can Purchase as a Porsche owner (or even just a fan), there's also a dedicated dashcam, which has now crossed over into a new generation. It's a multi-camera system that automatically records relevant driving and parking events, and it does all that in HDR, so that you can see exactly what just occurred.
There are plenty of reasons why you might want to install a dashcam in your car, and you don't have to own a Porsche in order to want to do so. You could be the best driver in the world and still find yourself in a situation where a dashcam would have come in handy. Besides, it's even more frustrating when something happens to your car when you're not around.
Then there's the matter of aesthetics. I don't think you want to spend six figures on a sports car only to stick a generic piece of plastic to your windshield. A lot of dashcams are extremely unaesthetic. You also don't want it obstructing your field of view in any way, but maybe that's just a pet peeve of mine. I don't even want any scented ornaments hanging from the rearview mirror.
Now, Porsche's new dashcam design is exactly what the doctor ordered, if what you're looking for is a discreet piece of tech. It also records what's happening inside the passenger compartment, which the previous model wasn't able to do.
The new device is positioned directly bellow/behind the interior rearview mirror, so it shouldn't interfere with your visibility . It even features an illuminated Porsche logo so that nobody can "accuse" you of having bought a generic aftermarket camera.
As far as image quality is concerned, we're dealing with QHD recordings with HDR tech, and there's also a polarizing filter that deals with reflections, which by the way, can be a problem on sunny days. Depending on the angle of the sun and the materials inside the vehicle, reflections on the windshield can render certain details in a recording more or less illegible - and being able to make out a license plate is one of the main selling points of any dashcam.
Photo: Porsche According to Porsche , the camera will produce clear, detailed footage even at higher speeds, which is important given the horsepower figures usually available to Porsche drivers. Then there's the G-sensor and radar, which detect events automatically and triggers a recording. Additional GPS information documents the exact location when the recording begins.
There are, of course, limitations regarding which cameras you can install on your Porsche. Owners of Cabriolet and Targa models will have to settle for just the front-facing unit, for obvious reasons.
As for connectivity, users can access all recordings, review events and adjust settings all from their My Porsche app.

The largest pharma deal since Pfizer’s 2023 Seagen acquisition has helped buoy M&A sentiment in the sector, which has become a safe haven for investors as the markets reel from the NVIDIA drama.
The Big Pharma sector finally has the mega-deal it was looking for, thanks to Sanofi’s splashy $41 billion acquisition of immunology-focused Insmed.
“The Sanofi-Insmed acquisition is a strong signal for continued momentum in biopharma M&A. At ~$41B, the transaction represents a substantial commitment from large pharma and, the largest deal of its kind since PFE/SGEN,” BMO Capital Markets wrote on Tuesday morning.
Pfizer spent a few billion more on Seagen in 2023, but since then the biggest buys have been in the $10-15 billion range. Before Insmed, the largest deal this year was AbbVie’s $10.9 billion Apogee Therapeutics buy in June . Sun Pharma also bought women’s health company Organon for $12.6 billion, however that deal falls slightly outside the typical biopharma sector.
The Insmed transaction comes as pharma enjoys a macro boost, particularly with the broader market roiled by controversy surrounding NVIDIA’s CEO drama.
“Recent pharma strength has been a bit of a rotation to safety,” Evan David Seigerman, managing director and head of BMO Capital Markets’ Healthcare Research, told BioSpace in an email. “The broader volatility has driven a flight to safety with pharma names.”
A strong third quarter earnings period helped buoy investor sentiment, Seigerman added.

Shares of Eli Lilly—which signed a $725 million deal to buy LoQus23 Therapeutics on Monday—popped 3% to $1,406 per share on Tuesday. Johnson & Johnson saw a more muted reaction but shares still rose nearly 2% to $273.97 apiece. And the companies at the center of the deal—Sanofi and Insmed—both had a great day at the markets .
M&A slowed in the third quarter , with many analysts, including Truist Securities, suggesting that the U.S. midterm elections had placed a pause on deal activity. Ahead of the vote, “few are willing to add risk,” Truist wrote in October.
But the fourth quarter tends to bring on a rush of deals as business development teams rush to get negotiations wrapped up by year end, Truist added. The last quarter typically has a higher deal count while the first quarter has higher value.
Sanofi’s Insmed takeover could flip that script this year. The transaction is not only the biggest deal of 2026 by about $30 billion, it’s the seventh largest biopharma acquisition of all time.
BioSpace , Annalee Armstrong
A battle to come?
The $175 per share bid for Insmed could bring some drama across the industry, as several analysts suggested there could be room for a competitive bid. Insmed’s shares peaked at $211 in December 2025—meaning the bid is 17% less.
But Truist Securities thinks Sanofi’s bid is safe.
“Our screen of large-cap pharma suggests few credible alternative buyers combine the financial capacity, strategic rationale and appetite for a $40B+ transaction,” the firm said in a Tuesday note. Plus, if a rival bidder were to come in, they would have to pay a $1.13 billion termination fee, Truist added.
J&J, Lilly, Roche and Novo technically have the cash to execute but none have expressed interest in a deal this size in this area.
“Merck arguably has the strongest combination of strategic need and M&A appetite ahead of Keytruda LOE, but a ~$40B acquisition would push leverage toward ~3x and sit well above management’s stated $1–15B M&A ‘sweet spot,’” Truist said.
Bristol Myers Squibb, similarly in need of some patent patch ups, has even greater financial constraints, the firm added.

“Taken together, we see limited strategic or financial rationale for a competing bidder to meaningfully top Sanofi’s $175/share offer, particularly after accounting for the $1.125 billion termination fee,” Truist said.
Alnylam investors, meanwhile, may see the Insmed transaction as a negative , Oppenheimer wrote on Tuesday. The company pays royalties for Amvuttra to Sanofi through a 2014 partnership. That tap could shut off after 2030, leading Oppemheimer to previously predict that Sanofi may buy out its long-time partner.
But all bets on that potential deal are now off with Insmed. “A $41B transaction shows Sanofi had the capacity to buy ALNY but chose Insmed instead,” the firm wrote. Alnylam has a market cap of $22 billion.
Alnylam saw a similar share increase to its peers on Tuesday, rising more than 5.5% to $164.75 as the biopharma tide rides on Sanofi’s big bet.

PitchBook has picked a handful of biotechs likely to go public soon—potentially even joining the already 2026’s bumper class—based on dealmaking activity, history and financial maturity.
2026 is already biotech’s biggest IPO year since the pandemic—and more still could join this year’s bumper class, including an RNA specialist riding the momentum of a mid-stage victory and a molecular glue developer backed by some of the industry’s biggest players.
That’s according to a recent analysis from the analytics firm PitchBook, which last month released a quarterly market report looking at, among other things, the companies most likely to launch an initial public offering (IPO).
The data firm used a proprietary machine learning model called VC Exit Predictor that evaluates a biotech’s likelihood of being acquired or going public based on metrics like dealmaking activity, financial maturity, number of crossover investors and the frequency and average size of funding rounds.
What PitchBook found is that the IPO window “remains open but selective, with a preference for companies with later-stage clinical assets,” Ben Zercher, senior biotech analyst, told BioSpace in an email. Already, more than 30 companies have taken the public plunge this year, up from just eight last year.

But digging into the data reveals that IPOs are “open mainly for larger, well-capitalized companies,” according to Zercher.
Such was the case for TRex Bio , which debuted in October after having been assessed by PitchBook as having a 97% likelihood of going public in the report. The immunoregulatory specialist brought in $84 million in series B money in November 2024 and $50 million in additional funds in January this year. TRex Bio is backed by the venture arms of some of the industry’s biggest players: Pfizer, Eli Lilly and Johnson & Johnson—the latter of which inked an immunology pact with the biotech in early 2022. TRex Bio’s IPO ultimately totaled $116.7 million.
Here, BioSpace looks at five other companies that, according to PitchBook, are poised to go public.

Ethris buoyed by maturity, patent portfolio, clinical momentum
Trailing TRex at a distant second is Ethris, which PitchBook assigned a 76% probability of going public.
The Munich-based drugmaker is advancing a pipeline of RNA-based medicines , led by the nasally administered ETH47, being studied for asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). ETH47 is designed to encode interferon lambda and elicit an immune response to prevent viral replication. Phase 2a findings released earlier this month showed that the asset boosted interferon lambda expression and lowered viral load by 40-fold on the second day after a nasal rhinovirus challenge in patients with asthma.
The study’s primary outcome was safety, and the latest readout showed that ETH47 was overall well tolerated, with no severe or serious side effects.
Aside from building up the clinical profile of its lead asset, Ethris has also steadily built capital in recent years, including a €30 million ($33.7 million) financing deal with the European Investment Bank in September to support the advancement of the biotech’s portfolio. Ethris in February announced it became part of a vaccine development consortium, alongside six other European companies, that stood to receive up to €148 million ($166.2 million) from the European Health and Digital Executive Agency.
PitchBook’s Exit Predictor model rates Ethris highly due to the biotech’s “IP portfolio built through mRNA development since 2009 and a long operating history,” Zercher told BioSpace, noting that Ethris’ recent financing efforts have been non-dilutive. “The company also has clinical momentum from positive topline Phase 2a data” for ETH47, he added.
Ethris’ overall rating “speaks more to long-term potential than to near-term timing,” Zercher said.
With hefty series C, Sling builds case for potentially first oral TED drug
Unlike Ethris, which has had no major VC round, Sling “fits the pre-IPO pattern more cleanly,” Zercher said. PitchBook assigned a 74% IPO probability to the eye disease-focused biotech.
The Michigan biotech in September brought in $123 million in a series C to power the development of linsitinib, an oral small-molecule IGF-1R inhibitor for thyroid eye disease (TED). Concurrent with the fundraising round, Sling launched the Phase 3 ORBIT trial, primarily looking at the asset’s ability to ease the abnormal bulging of the eyes (proptosis) that is characteristic of the condition as compared to placebo. ORBIT is currently enrolling with initial data expected in 2028.
Data from the Phase 2b/3 LIDS trial demonstrated a 52% proptosis response rate at 24 weeks—the study’s primary outcome—in patients treated with linsitinib, according to a January 2025 readout . If linsitinib clears all late-stage and regulatory hurdles, it could be the first oral TED drug to hit the market, according to Sling.
Sling launched in June 2022 with $35 million in series A capital and a licensing deal with Astellas Pharma, from which the startup got linsitinib. The biotech hasn’t disclosed any other clinical candidates .
Sling is backed by Forbion, TPG Life Sciences and Sectoral Asset Management.

Big Pharma-backed TRIANA still in early development
Pasting together a pipeline of molecular glues is TRIANA Biomedicines, which according to PitchBook’s analysis has a 73% IPO likelihood.
Much of the Boston biotech’s momentum comes from its strong financing history. In 2022, TRIANA launched with a $110 million series A to advance molecular glue therapies for cancer, according to a news release at the time. TRIANA conducted a $120 million in series B in December 2025.
Across the two funding rounds, TRIANA has garnered support from some of the industry’s biggest players, including Pfizer Ventures, Regeneron Ventures and Surveyor Capital. Aside from the participation of its venture arm, Pfizer in October 2024 paid $49 million upfront to partner with TRIANA for molecular glue therapies for various disease areas. This agreement includes milestone payments that could top $1.5 billion.
TRIANA was seeded by RA Capital Management and Atlas Venture, which have continued to provide funding.
Also adding to TRIANA’s list of backers is Johnson & Johnson, which in January inked a research collaboration with the biotech to discover and develop molecular glues for cancer indications. Financial details were not disclosed.
Despite its strong financial backing, TRIANA’s pipeline is still relatively young for public prime time. The biotech’s lead asset, the oral ALK-targeting drug candidate TRI-611 , is in Phase 1/2 development for non-small cell lung cancer. The rest of TRIANA’s assets have yet to enter the clinic.
After in vivo pivot, EXUMA back to preclinical development
With a 56% chance of going public, according to PitchBook, is EXUMA Biotech, a Florida-based specialist in CAR T therapies.
The company—previously named F1 Oncology before rebranding in March 2020 —raised $37 million in a series A in January 2017, $19 million in a series B in March 2020 and $41 million in a series B2 in December 2021. In an SEC filing earlier this year, EXUMA disclosed that it had raised $70 million in equity, Zercher told BioSpace , adding to the company’s IPO momentum.
EXUMA originally focused on advancing autologous CAR T therapies—treatments that make use of cells drawn from the patients themselves. In January 2025, EXUMA reported data from a completed Phase 1 data for an autologous HER2-targeting CAR T candidate, touting no dose-limiting toxicities or serious adverse events related to the asset. In the 12-patient study, EXUMA documented “deep” partial response at 36 weeks in patients with HER2-positive stage IV solid tumors.
EXUMA has since pivoted to in vivo approaches , “an area drawing strong pharma interest ,” Zercher said, pushing the biotech it back to the preclinical stage. EXUMA’s in vivo program has yet to enter the clinic, and the company hasn’t publicly disclosed a timeline for clinical development.
Lilly partner Juvena still in early development for muscular diseases
Capping off this list is Juvena Therapeutics, which comes in just behind EXUMA with a 55% probability of going public, according to PitchBook’s analysis.
Juvena, which made BioSpace ’s 2024 NextGen Class , came onto the scene in November 2022 with $41 million in series A money and a mission to study the potential of secreted proteins to treat chronic and age-related conditions. The California company added to its pot in January this year, with a $33.5 million series B.
Juvena counts incretin heavyweight Eli Lilly among its supporters, which participated in the biotech’s series B and in June 2025 paid an undisclosed upfront amount and equity investment to partner on therapies to improve muscle health and body composition. The deal includes milestones though a specific amount wasn’t disclosed.
Juvena’s pipeline is led by JUV-161 , an investigational IGF2-derived engineered protein therapeutic. The asset is being developed for myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1), muscle atrophy, sarcopenia and other muscular dystrophies. JUV-161 recently completed Phase 1 development, but the biotech has yet to disclose findings. Enrollment in a Phase 1/2 study for muscular atrophy is ongoing. The FDA in January 2024 awarded JUV-161 the orphan drug designation of DM1.

Lexus Announces New Special Edition for the Best-Selling LBX Compact Crossover on the Old Continent
9 photos
Photo: Lexus
The premium Japanese automaker Lexus has revealed a special edition - it doesn't even carry a distinct name - for the LBX model, which is their best-selling model in the compact crossover SUV range.
The company hasn’t been very diligent when it comes to its European affairs: back in July, they showcased the Lexus LFA Concept at the 2026 Goodwood Festival of Speed with the world's first dynamic drives; early in September, they announced the “significant mid-lifecycle upgrade ” for the NX, and also launched the international sales of the Lexus LY680 luxury yacht – though the boat was actually exhibited at the Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show in America.
Earlier this month, the brand also revealed the refreshed Lexus NX at the Nitto ATP Finals tournament in Turin, Italy, as a counterpoint to the “climax of the elite men’s international tennis season.” Lexus was a Platinum Partner and the Official Automotive Partner of the Nitto ATP Finals for the fourth year in a row, which is why the Lexus NX enjoyed a high-profile European reveal at the Nitto ATP Finals, which finished on November 22.
Now, the company is moving down the lineup to the subcompact luxury crossover SUV , with the B-segment LBX , primarily developed for Japan and Europe and offered since the 2024 model year, showcasing the first details for the model’s new special edition. The regular Lexus LBX is offered on the TNGA-B architecture shared with the Toyota Yaris Cross and has both ICE and hybrid versions.
The Lexus brand says the LBX has quickly become its best-selling model in Europe thanks to a combination of compact dimensions and entry-level pricing, and now they want to make it even more enticing with a fresh special edition. “The LBX has quickly established itself as a highly stylish leader for Lexus, (…) this new special edition will maintain the model’s reputation for distinctive good looks and authentic luxury features, matched to highly efficient and refined performance,” said Andre Schmidt, Head of Lexus Europe.
The features offered with the special edition include a new and exclusive Skylight Blue exterior color or an alternate Cement Grey bi-tone paint finish, paired with a black roof and pillars plus a jet-black treatment for elements such as the lower moldings front and back or the “resolute look” bar. There are also matte black finished 18-inch alloy wheels along with a “laser-etched-like striped pattern that creates a subtle L motif on the rear pillars.”
Moving inside, the cabin gains black semi-aniline leather upholstery with “ochre stitching along the seams and hatched embroidery across the seatbacks.” There is also highlighting stitchwork on the center console and door panels, plus a leather-wrapped steering wheel and shift lever. Additionally, Lexus adds that the special edition is based on the high specification LBX Emotion trim level.
That means the limited series comes with perks like heated front sports seats with eight-way power adjustment and memory settings, the Lexus e-Latch door operation, which is unique to the LBX in the class, plus paddle shifters for additional power control.
There is also a 12.3-inch digital instrument display for the driver, scuff plates, plus the 9.8-inch LexusLink Connect multimedia package featuring wireless smartphone integration, along with the Lexus Safety System + portfolio of active safety and driver assistance systems. Lexus announced that first deliveries are coming in early 2027.

But that wasn’t the most enticing recent announcement, actually.
Instead, the company has officially kicked off the teaser campaign for the second iteration of the Porsche 718 Boxster – sometime during the first quarter of 2027, the brand will unleash its first all-electric two-door sports car, the new Porsche 718. They start with the Boxster, as the roadster is always more enticing when you’re out of the woods from a tough winter, of course.
Most importantly, the company again shared some of the most important details regarding the new model, which is going to be all-electric – both the Boxster and the Cayman sibling. For example, many of the parts are inspired by the Porsche 911, and the car will retain its classic mid-engine configuration – although the company has now placed an E-Core in there rather than a boxer engine.
So, the new all-electric Porsche 718 Boxster will have the 800-volt battery pack located directly behind the car's two seats, where the ICE usually resides for this sports car application, allowing for a 40/60 weight distribution. The shared 911 parts include the steering with rear-axle setup, braking system, and the electronically controlled limited-slip differential, among others.
Porsche hasn’t offered the full numbers breakdown for the power and weight, but said the new 718 Boxster will sprint to 62 mph in less than three seconds and hit a classic top speed of 155 mph (250 kph). There’s also E-Shift, a virtual gearbox, borrowed this time from the Taycan, and a fake six-cylinder boxer engine sound borrowed from the 981-generation Boxster GTS.
As for the looks, the prototype car shown by Porsche is dressed in a funky black and white topographic map wrap featuring red accents, which conceals most of the styling. No worries, though, as the recent Porsche teaser immediately triggered the activation of a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators who stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI and unwrapped the 718 Boxster EV.
More precisely, Sugar Chow, the virtual artist better known as " sugardesign_1 " on social media, has decided to CGI-present his vision for the all-new Porsche 718 Boxster Electric, and now it’s easy to see it in all its glory, including details like the gilled front side air intakes, the Taycan and Macan Electric or Cayenne Electric-inspired headlights, the new red and illuminated Porsche script placed between the slim LED taillights, or the new signature element on the trunk lid. Lexus Launches New TZ in the UK, Here’s How Much the Premium Toyota Highlander Costs
12 photos
Photo: Lexus
Do you remember the Lexus TZ ? Well, you likely do, as it premiered half a year ago. The model is now getting ready to go on sale in the United Kingdom, and the company’s local arm has just announced the pricing and specifications for this market.
The lineup comprises three grades and two powertrain options. The base model is the 450e Premium Plus, and it has an on-the-road starting price of 74,895 pounds (equal to $97,945). It has 304 hp (308 ps/227 kW) to play with, and benefits from a 14-inch multimedia display, a head-up display, a panoramic sunroof, a digital rearview mirror, heated and ventilated front seats, a digital key, Intelligent Parking Assist, and other things.
From 81,495 pounds ($106,575), the mid-range Takumi becomes available. This model brings not only more oomph, as it has 397 hp (402 ps/296 kW) on tap, but also extra gear. Some of the highlights include the 22-inch wheels, premium synthetic suede upholstery, a multi-color ambient lighting system, radiant front heaters, a higher-quality acoustic window glass, electrically-adjustable seats, Dynamic Rear Steering, and Interactive Manual Drive.
Photo: Lexus Sitting at the very top of the 2027 Lexus TZ family in the United Kingdom is the Takumi Design. It builds on the mid-range flavor, offers the same powertrain, and comes with bespoke 22-inch wheels, a two-tone exterior design, Bright Bamboo trim details on the inside, and a premium sound system from Mark Levinson with 21 speakers. Pricing for this trim level kicks off at 83,095 pounds ($108,670).
All versions of the new electric crossover benefit from all-wheel drive (Direct4), and feature a 95.8 kWh battery pack feeding the electric motors. The model is assembled in Japan and the United States, and from 2027, it will hit production in China, too. It shares numerous nuts and bolts with the Toyota Highlander , hence the reference in the title, and the TNGA-K construction is also used on the Camry, Avalon, RAV4, Sienna, Venza, Lexus NX, RX, ES, Subaru Getaway, and other models.
Lexus will kick off the sales of the TZ in spring 2027, and as you already know, the model is also marketed in the United States of America. Two trim levels are available on our shores, the Premium and the Luxury, which officially kick off at $64,050 (equal to £48,970) and $80,550 (£61,585), respectively, excluding destination, options, and dealer fees. Both have 308 hp on tap, and while the former has a manufacturer-estimated driving range of 253 miles (407 km), the latter can travel 279 miles (449 km) on a full charge.
The 2027 Lexus TZ Premium will be available in the United States of America starting in late 2026, and for the Luxury trim level, interested parties will have to wait until early 2027.

Harley-Davidson Sends Three Fresh ST Baggers Our Way, Road King and More Are Back for 2027
6 photos
Photo: Harley-Davidson
For years now, American bike maker Harley-Davidson has gotten us used to releasing the bikes for the new model year in January. While this habit still stands, the Milwaukee crew went off program this week and announced the arrival of three new motorcycles for 2027, but also a few details on what we are to expect in the coming months.
At the core of Harley-Davidson's announcement remain the three new Grand American Touring models being offered. Not new in the sense that they are just now entering the lineup, but new in that, despite being based on existing bikes, are still fresh enough to get hearts pumping.
The trio comprises ST versions of the Road Glide , Street Glide, and the returning Road King. They are very closely related, as they share many of their component parts, including the Showa suspension system and the Brembo braking hardware.
Also common is the powertrain, which would be the Milwaukee-Eight 117 High Output engine, modified to deliver 12 percent more horsepower than the standard Milwaukee-Eight 117 engine. That would be a total of 115 hp for the two Glides, and slightly more, 117 hp, for the Road King.
Photo: Harley-Davidson The Road is perhaps the most exciting of the bunch, as it makes a comeback at the end of a relatively brief hiatus. And it comes back with visual changes as well, including a redesigned headlamp nacelle, reshaped bodywork, and a low-profile console.
All three motorcycles in their 2027 model year guise are already listed as available on the bike maker's U.S. configurator, but only one of them, the Road King, also shows a price sticker – that would be $24,999 for this two-wheeler. We'll keep an eye out for when pricing for the two Glides becomes public.
The three new STs are part of the company's plan to expand its offering for the new model year, but they are not the only changes that were announced. As you'll see below, there is talk of new colors, a new special collection, and hints of a bunch of insane CVO models.
When it comes to the colors it offers for its bikes, Harley announced that, at the request of customers, Vivid Black now becomes the base paint color for most of the lineup, kicking the current Dark Billiard Gray from this role.
Photo: Harley-Davidson Also new is something called the Lunar Divide, a paint scheme that brings together Vivid Black and Black Denim for a two-tone approach, and offsets that with the help of Medium Red pinstripes. If you like the idea, don't get your hopes up, as this design will only be offered for the Low Rider S and Low Rider ST models.
The new Lunar Divide paint scheme from Harley-Davidson Factory Custom Paint & Graphics, available only for the Low Rider® S and Low Rider® ST motorcycles, is composed of a dynamic split Vivid Black/Black Denim two-tone with a Medium Red pinstripe parting line executed in a reverse scallop design.'
I mentioned something about a special collection earlier in the story. It's called Iron & Ink, and it is a way of painting the bodies of some Harley bikes while at the same time paying tribute to the tattoo culture and its creations.
Iron & Ink uses deep red Oxblood Metallic as a base color, and matches that with a dedicated windscreen and hand-crafted detailing of new and iconic elements, including the Bar & Shield logo and the V-twin engine silhouette. Harley promises references to the bison of the Black Hills and the water tower at Harley's Juneau Avenue HQ, among others.
Photo: Harley-Davidson The special paint job will only be available on the Street Glide and Road Glide bikes in black trim, and only 2,000 of them will be made for each of the models. The offering is part of the Enthusiast Collection and will set people back $27,999 for the Street and $28,999 for the Road.
Last but not least, Harley mentioned a thing or two about the CVO lineup for the 2027 model year, without going too deep into the details. We are to expect a collection of five limited-production performance machines: the CVO Road Glide, CVO Street Glide ST , CVO Road Glide ST, CVO Street Glide Limited, and CVO Street Glide 3 Limited.
Harley let loose the fact that the bikes are packed with new Screamin’ Eagle/Ohlins front and rear suspension parts and Brembo Hypure braking components. There will be six exclusive new design and paint schemes on the table, but we're not being told anything about them yet.
The Harley cruiser range gets an upgrade as well, with an eight-model strong family now on the table. It is throwing into the fight the Super Glide that was born earlier this year as a limited-production bike, but is now turning into a global model, the Deadwood, the Low Rider S and ST, and, of course, the almighty Breakout, Heritage Classic, Fat Boy, and Street Bob.

Not long ago, we got pretty happy that, at long last, the good folks over at the racing-focused ' Import 2 Race ' channel on YouTube finally went back to spending some quality time around their usual venue, which is Island Dragway in Great Meadows, New Jersey, a very nice racetrack that’s been around since it was established back in 1960.

2027 Hyundai Tucson Throws in First-Ever Hybrid XRT Pro, ICE Also on the Table
8 photos
Photo: Hyundai
It's not long now until 2026 ends, and carmakers are wrapping up the finishing touches for what they'll offer in the new year. For Hyundai, this year's story seems to end, and next year's seems to begin with the refreshed Tucson SUV.
Now in its fifth generation, the compact crossover wearing the name of an Arizona city comes along with fewer changes than most would have expected, yet enough of them to keep people interested in what it has to offer.
At the core of the upgrades sits a revised powertrain lineup, consisting of both a version powered exclusively by an internal combustion engine and a hybrid one. Only these two are on the table for the new model year.
For people who still cherish the old way of powering a ride, the South Koreans throw in a 1.6-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine tied to an eight-speed automatic transmission with a torque converter. It's not insanely powerful, but not a letdown either – it is rated at 184 hp at 6,000 rpm and 195 lb.-ft. torque between 1,600 - 4,500 rpm.
The other powertrain on the table is the hybrid that bundles together a 1.6-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine with a permanent magnet motor and a lithium-ion battery sized at 1.49 kWh.
Photo: Hyundai The system, known internally as TMED-II, is rated at 233 horsepower (64 hp from the electric motor) at 6,000 rpm and 280 lb.-ft. torque from 1,500 rpm to 4,000 rpm. A six-speed automatic transmission is on deck to properly handle that. On select and yet undisclosed trim levels, this setup is said to return 42 mpg (5.6 liters/100 km) fuel consumption.
Specifically for the hybrid version, Hyundai imagines something called the E-Traction system, meant to optimize driving torque and bring down wheel slip levels. There is also a Stay Mode function on deck for the hybrids, which allows owners to run air conditioning, heating, audio, and device charging even when the engine is off.
The powertrains being offered are hidden inside a body that's not only redesigned, but also bigger than before, in all aspects that matter. At 185 inches long, it has grown by 2.3 inches, while at the same time becoming 1.6 inches wider, now at 75 inches.
Its height has grown too, not by much, but the extra 0.7 inches, without roof rails, takes the roof 66.3 inches off the ground. The new dimensions required a rethink of the rear door opening angles, which have grown from 73 to 83 degrees.
Photo: Hyundai The increased dimensions translate into additional interior space for cargo and passengers. In numbers, that would be 40.8 inches of front headroom, 41.9 inches of rear legroom, and 57.9 inches of front shoulder room.
Hyundai's boldest SUV ever, as the carmaker itself likes to describe it, also throws new colors on the table. For the bodywork, there will be four of them (Ranger Green Pearl, Summit Blue Pearl, Driftwood Gray Metallic/Matte, and Red Rock Orange Pearl), while the cabin can be specced in several hues, including Black Gray and two-tone brown.
The SUVs are equipped across the range with Hyundai's new Pleos Connect solution running the Gleo AI. Derived from the Android Automotive OS, the system interacts with drivers through one or two infotainment screens (12.9-inch or 17.0-inch). The instrument cluster can be displayed on a 9.9-inch screen.
The highlight of Hyundai's new Tucson family must be the XRT Pro, the first version of this kind powered by a hybrid powertrain. It sets itself apart from the rest of the range by being all-wheel drive (the wheels are 18 inches across) and equipped with all-terrain tires and an increased ground clearance (8.3 inches, 1.2 inches more than the base ICE SUV).
Photo: Hyundai Being meant for use off the beaten path, the Tucson XRT Pro is clad with protection hardware all around, including lower body panels with forged-carbon-inspired patterns. There are even front recovery hooks for when things turn tricky.
Something called the X-Trek+ system is what makes the XRT Pro really special. Used for the first time on this model, it acts as a real-time terrain difficulty assessment technology that looks at traction and low-traction conditions.
The system is meant to help drivers by visually guiding them on the best path ahead with green, red, and orange stuck scores. In a nutshell, it's something that tells people where to drive next so that they don't need to use the recovery hooks I mentioned earlier.
In extreme situations, the X-Trek+ works with the target speed control feature that manages acceleration and braking while off-road, allowing the SUV to travel at the speed set by the driver, up to a maximum speed of 15 mph (24 kph).
Hyundai already lists the 2027 Tucson on its North American configurators, but that doesn't mean the SUV can be ordered right now. The carmaker hasn't yet released pricing on the vehicle, as that is kept until closer to the launch date, which will be the first quarter of 2027 for the ICE-powered vehicles and the second quarter for the hybrid.

Ineos Is Moving to America, Might Sell Its Plant to Chinese Auto Giant
6 photos
Photo: BYD
BYD is trying to gain territory outside Asia, and Europe is a solid market that it has been counting on over the past few years. To extend its footprint, the Chinese auto giant is planning to operate yet another factory, and the one that Ineos will leave empty is a serious option.
BYD has entered exclusive negotiations for the acquisition of the plant that Ineos Automotive has been using since its inception. Ineos bought the Hambach factory from Mercedes-Benz on December 8, 2020, for an undisclosed sum.
Just before putting the plant up for sale in 2020, Mercedes-Benz invested roughly 470 million to 500 million euros ($515.5 million to $548.5 million) to upgrade Hambach to build larger electric crossovers like the Mercedes EQB. Ineos reports it has invested more than 700 million euros ($766 million) into the Hambach facility overall, including upgrades to the paint shop and automated body shop.
Now, Ineos has announced plans to relocate production of the Grenadier SUV and Quartermaster pickup truck to the United States by 2028. The move makes sense since the United States accounts for roughly 70% of Ineos Automotive's global sales.
Photo: BYD Producing vehicles in the U.S. will allow Ineos Automotive to bypass U.S. import tariffs on European vehicles, including the 25% 'chicken tax' on imported pickup trucks like the Quartermaster, which has been in place since 1964.
The automaker has reportedly shortlisted several locations across the United States and will announce the final manufacturing site within the next few months. Ineos has not confirmed whether it will buy an existing assembly plant, build a new facility, or partner with a contract manufacturer.
While preparing for the relocation, Ineos is negotiating the sale of its Hambach plant with BYD, Electrek reports . Located in northeastern France, near the German border, the factory currently employs 900 to 1,000 workers and has an annual capacity of about 30,000 vehicles.
Ineos confirmed that if the sale closes, it will continue to build the Grenadier and the Quartermaster at Hambach for the "medium term," until its U.S. production kicks off. Neither automaker has disclosed the financial terms of the potential deal.
Photo: Ineos Automotive BYD’s European car manufacturing is centered on its new factory in Szeged, Hungary , which is currently transitioning from trial runs to mass production, scheduled to begin in late 2026 or early 2027. The facility has an initial annual capacity of roughly 150,000 vehicles.
While the factory in Hungary is set to build the compact Dolphin Surf hatchback, along with the Atto 2 SUV, BYD has recently hit a legal roadblock with another model intended for the region.
On November 20, a preliminary relief judge at the District Court of The Hague issued an EU-wide injunction barring BYD from producing, importing, marketing, or selling its seven-seat Ti7 SUV, ruling that the vehicle infringes registered European design rights for the Land Rover Defender.
Building vehicles inside Hungary and France, which are both European Union member states, will help BYD qualify for upcoming EU Made in Europe rules, unlocking EV subsidies for its models and avoiding import tariffs.
Photo: BYD If the deal with Ineos goes through, BYD becomes the second Chinese automaker to purchase an existing European car factory. Back in 2024, Chery Automobile acquired the former Nissan factory in Barcelona, Spain, via a joint venture with Ebro-EV Motors, to build cars in Europe.
Both BYD and Chery hold talks to buy Ford’s Saarlouis factory in Germany in 2023, but those negotiations collapsed. Meanwhile, Ford officially ended Focus production and closed vehicle assembly at the plant in November 2025.

A look at how Summit Therapeutics framed ivonescimab’s clinical results compared with how the FDA weighed the evidence behind its application.
“[M]ore time, more possibilities, and a better future.” Those words appeared near the beginning of Summit Therapeutics’ Nov. 15 announcement that the FDA had declined to approve ivonescimab for patients with EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer. Drawing on her experience as a cancer survivor, Summit’s co-CEO Maky Zanganeh spoke about what another treatment option could mean for patients and their families. Had it been approved, ivonescimab would have been the first PD-1xVEGF bispecific to hit the U.S. market.
The announcement acknowledged that the Phase 3 HARMONi trial had missed its overall survival (OS) endpoint and that the FDA considered the progression-free survival (PFS) benefit insufficient to support approval. The full letter , published two days later, detailed additional concerns about the trial’s design, safety and applicability to U.S. patients.
The agency could not establish whether the PFS result applied to U.S. patients. Of the 275 progression or death events in the prespecified analysis, 257 (93%) occurred in patients enrolled in China. The FDA had flagged the enrollment as a potential problem in March 2023 and again at the May 2025 pre-filing meeting. Those concerns remained unresolved when Summit submitted its application.
The FDA also called the PFS gain “modest” in light of the added risks, including serious immune-related toxicities and toxicities associated with VEGF inhibition. It also treated the posthoc analyses as exploratory, with the survival analysis further limited by different regional data cutoffs. The agency recommended that Summit submit results from a new, adequate and well-controlled multiregional trial.
In effect, the FDA is asking for a redo.
This wasn’t the outcome Summit had hoped for. As a healthcare investment banking professional, I was curious about how the company had presented its clinical results over the years, so I revisited its ivonescimab announcements. “Summit made a compelling case for the drug’s potential, while leaving the assessment of remaining uncertainties to the market.”
Lung cancer
Summit’s rejection letter reveals FDA’s deeper concerns about trial design, safety
Summit Therapeutics was warned twice by the FDA that the Phase 3 trial used to support the application for ivonescimab did not include patients that accurately represented the American population.
November 18, 2026
·
3 min read
·
Annalee Armstrong
Read more
A $500 million head start
In December 2022, Summit agreed to pay Akeso $500 million upfront for exclusive rights to develop and commercialize ivonescimab in the U.S., Canada, Europe and Japan. By then, Akeso had largely finished enrolling patients in its Chinese Phase 3 trial, HARMONi-A. The companies carried eligible patients from that trial into the multiregional HARMONi study. Akeso CEO Yu Xia later described the approach as “a bit of a shortcut” ( translated from Chinese ). It saved time, but by the primary analysis, median follow-up was 32.7 months for Asian patients and just 9.2 months for Western patients.
While HARMONi was still enrolling patients in the West, Summit had a result from a separate Phase 3 trial to share. After HARMONi-2 showed a PFS advantage over Merck’s mega-blockbuster PD-1 inhibitor Keytruda (pembrolizumab) in a China-based trial, some media outlets dubbed ivonescimab a “Keytruda killer.” Indeed, the headline of Akeso’s press release opened with “ ivonescimab monotherapy decisively beats pembrolizumab .” The advantage was in PFS in a first-line lung cancer trial , but the data came from China, leaving open whether those results would be sufficient to support an FDA approval.
Those data came a year later, when HARMONi, the trial behind Summit’s U.S. application, also met its PFS endpoint. This time, however, overall survival was a primary endpoint as well—and it missed. When the conversation turned to that endpoint, Zanganeh characterized the missed threshold as a matter of decimal places.
Lung cancer
Summit, Akeso’s ivonescimab bests Merck’s Keytruda in China trial—again
New Phase 3 data show that Summit Therapeutics and Akeso’s PD-1/VEGF therapy improved overall survival in patients with a type of lung cancer as compared to Merck’s Keytruda but the results will need to be replicated in non-Chinese patients.
September 3, 2026
·
2 min read
·
Annalee Armstrong
Read more
‘You’re playing with the penny numbers’
In HARMONi, median OS was 16.8 months with ivonescimab plus chemotherapy and 14 months with placebo plus chemotherapy. The hazard ratio was 0.79, suggesting a 21% lower estimated hazard of death, but the p-value was non-significant at 0.057. In the Western subgroup, the OS hazard ratio was 0.98 at the primary analysis, showing little difference between the treatment groups at that point.
At Goldman Sachs’ healthcare conference in June 2025, analyst Salveen Richter asked what might explain HARMONi’s failure to achieve statistical significance on OS. Zanganeh compared the 0.057 p-value with the standard significance cutoff of 0.05. “You’re playing with the penny numbers,” she said.
But the trial was designed with a stricter significance threshold than the conventional 0.05, requiring a p-value below 0.0448 to meet its OS endpoint. And the question wasn’t just how close Summit came to statistical significance, but whether the survival data were convincing enough for the FDA. Summit acknowledged at the same conference that OS had been included as a primary endpoint at the FDA’s request. The FDA’s eventual decision showed how consequential that missed endpoint would become.
‘Two 0.76s’ bridge
With longer follow-up , the Western OS hazard ratio improved, moving from 0.98 to 0.84, then to 0.76. Around the 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer, Summit described the Western and Asian survival results as “ consistent .” Akeso’s latest 2026 interim report went further, saying efficacy, safety and long-term survival benefits had been “consistently and thoroughly validated through multiple Phase 3 clinical studies across China, North America and Europe.”
In that updated analysis , the global and Western OS hazard ratios both rounded to 0.76, but the underlying data told a more complicated story. The extended follow-up covered only 165 Western patients, while data for the 273 Asian patients, representing 62% of the trial population, remained locked at the April 2025 cutoff. The global hazard ratio of 0.76, with a nominal p-value of 0.0151, therefore combined updated Western data with older Asian data. In the Western subgroup alone, the same hazard ratio came with a much wider 95% confidence interval (0.52–1.10), which still crossed 1.0—the point indicating no difference in death risk between treatment groups. While the point estimate favored ivonescimab, the Western data could not rule out no survival benefit or even a modest increase in the hazard of death.
Summit’s latest 10-Q SEC filing before the FDA decision put the company’s and the agency’s views in consecutive paragraphs. Summit said it believed the regimen offered a favorable benefit-risk profile despite the survival miss. In the next paragraph, it disclosed that the FDA considered a statistically significant OS benefit necessary to support approval and that the PFS results might be insufficient.

“Nothing changes”
In November 2025, Summit counted “four positive Phase III studies after four Phase III readouts.” A year later, in the announcement of the FDA decision, Summit’s chair and co-CEO Robert Duggan cited five—HARMONi counted because it met the PFS endpoint, but fell short on the OS endpoint central to the FDA’s decision. As for his confidence in ivonescimab, he said “nothing changes.”
There were also reasons for optimism about ivonescimab’s broader development program. About six weeks before the FDA decision, AstraZeneca completed a $2 billion equity investment in Summit and agreed to explore combinations of ivonescimab with several antibody-drug conjugates. In first-line lung cancer, HARMONi-3 is testing ivonescimab plus chemotherapy head-to-head against Keytruda plus chemotherapy.
With several clinical trials still underway, ivonescimab’s story is far from over. As new results emerge, the focus will be on what they tell us about the drug’s potential, how much confidence to place in them and what remains uncertain.

If you’ve ever looked at a classic 1929 Bentley Blower and thought, “That looks great, but could it be smaller, electric, and somehow still cost six figures?” then good news: your car has arrived.
Hedley Studios has completed the first 25 production Bentley Blower Jnrs, with the hand-built electric mini-cars now heading to customers. Deliveries are beginning in the UK before expanding across Europe.
The Blower Jnr is an officially licensed collaboration with Bentley, recreating the famous 1929 Bentley 4½ Liter Supercharged Team Car No. 2 at 85% scale. Unlike many scaled-down collector cars, though, this isn’t merely an expensive toy for cruising around your estate. It’s actually road legal.
In the UK and EU, the Blower Jnr is homologated as an L7e quadricycle, reaching over 50 mph (80 km/h) and offering a certified 75-mile (120 km) range. A separate US program is also planned, though it’s not clear exactly what classification the mini-EV would receive stateside.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Underneath the delightfully old-school bodywork is a decidedly newer 48V electric drivetrain producing 31 hp (23 kW). The electric motor sits across the rear axle, while batteries and power electronics are packaged underneath the car.
The carbon-fiber tub rides on a steel frame with leaf springs and period-style friction dampers, while Brembo disc brakes handle stopping duties up front.
There are some particularly fun details, too. The charging port is hidden inside a recreation of the original Bentley’s supercharger housing, while modern necessities like indicators, headlights, and even a reversing camera have been incorporated without ruining the 1929 aesthetic.
The first 25 cars are part of a nearly sold-out run of 99 First Editions. Another 250 configurable cars will follow, bringing total production to just 349 units.
And “Jnr” definitely doesn’t mean junior pricing. Configurable cars start at £112,500 before taxes – roughly $148,000 at current exchange rates.
Then again, if you’re buying a hand-built miniature electric Bentley, value probably wasn’t the first thing on your mind.

The South Korean automaker Hyundai has been very busy in November – mostly thanks to a couple of its most important and popular models, the all-new Elantra compact sedan and the Tucson compact crossover SUV.
The South Korean automaker has made it easier for all of us to track the modifications to the 2027MY lineup in the United States by compiling a list of changes for them earlier this month, confirming the arrival of both the all-new Tucson and the Elantra, plus the feisty Ioniq 6 N.
At the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show, the attention was focused on the all-new eighth-generation 2027 Elantra and 2028 Elantra Hybrid, but the company also announced the all-new i30 Sedan for Australia, which is the local version of the global Elantra – and it will even supersede the Sonata, which is bowing out of the local market.
Back to North America, Hyundai recently announced the pricing for the Ioniq 6 N for the Canadian market, and the performance EV almost costs as much as a BMW M2 Coupe! In the United States, meanwhile, the South Korean company has revealed all the juicy details and full specifications (sans pricing) for the Tucson ICE and Hybrid, as well as the XRT PRO adventure version.

WARSAW, Poland — Czech jet engine producer PBS Aerospace aims to expand its manufacturing capacity in the United States, targeting at least a twofold increase in its production capacity there, according to senior company representatives.
Jan Havránek, PBS Aerospace’s chief government relations and strategy officer, told Defense News that is because the business is booming due to a rising demand for compact propulsion systems used in drones and cruise missiles.
“Everybody wants to build drones and missiles that are fast, fly far, and they want to have them now. That puts scale and quality at the center of the conversation,” Havránek said. “Global conflicts, including the war in Ukraine, have made clear how important it is for the United States to have a reliable domestic supply of these engines, and the market is moving quickly.”
While continuing to produce engines at its factory in Velká Bíteš, in the Czech Republic, PBS Aerospace expanded its American presence in September 2025 with the launch of a plant in Roswell, Georgia. The manufacturing facility was opened as part of a $20 million investment.
“We’re building engines in America, for America,” Havránek said. “Our Georgia facility serves the U.S. market first and foremost, with the U.S. government as our end customer. We supply engines to prime contractors that deliver systems to the Department of War, and we’re proud to help strengthen the U.S. defense industrial base and bring critical manufacturing back onshore.”
In the U.S., the group’s partners include Lockheed Martin and Pratt & Whitney.
To meet rising demand, PBS Aerospace plans to increase its Roswell facility’s annual output to between 10,000 and 20,000 engines over the next three years.
“For next year, we’re looking at up to 5,000 engines to be produced in America,” he said.
With the manufacturing ramp-up in mind, PBS Aerospace is planning to allocate around $100 million to boost its capacity in Roswell, according to Havránek.
Some of the company’s most sought-after products include the TJ40-G1, a compact jet engine that weighs 3.4 kg (7.5 pounds) and delivers up to 425 N of thrust, as indicated by data from the manufacturer.

Android Auto 18.2 Starts Rolling Out With a Big Navigation Change for Wide Screens
13 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution/Google
How about that? An Android Auto feature that actually includes a front-facing change. The all-new Android Auto version 18.2 , which is now rolling out through the Google Play Store, includes a navigation change that makes it easier to interact with apps on an infotainment unit with a wide screen.
At the moment, the Android Auto interface shows the navigation buttons at the top of the screen. This means that you must tap these buttons to interact with your apps, such as Spotify and YouTube Music, and access certain features like the music library or the recently-played tunes.
Doing this from the driver’s seat isn’t exactly the most convenient thing to do, especially on a device with a wide screen, as you must have to lean to your right specifically to be able to tap the option that is farther from you.
That’s why Google is changing this in Android Auto 18.2 by moving the navigation bar to the left, therefore bringing all options closer to the driver.
Google is tweaking the entire Android Auto UI - and the apps running on top of it - to use the screen estate more effectively. While the navigation bar is now displayed in a vertical position on the left of the screen, the music artwork and the rest of the details, including the name of the songs, are now displayed across the entire UI. The thumbnails are larger, and in so many ways, this approach makes perfect sense because all your information is much easier to read.
There’s also a mini-player that remains on top of everything else on the screen, so you can control the music playback directly from this menu, without having to open the entire Now Playing interface.
The new UI has also been updated by the dialer in the Phone app. Instead of dedicated options to access favorites, recents, contacts, and the dial pad at the top of the screen, you can now just tap these options in the vertical sidebar that appears when you launch the app.
The same approach should soon make its way to all apps on Android Auto, though for now, they appear to be limited to media apps and the dialer. Only devices with wide resolutions are getting the new navigation app, though there’s no doubt they would come in handy on all units, as the essential options would be easier to reach from the driver’s seat.
Photo: AndroidAuthority Google appears to be fine-tuning the Android Auto interface at a time when the company is also giving the finishing touches to the major update it promised in the spring. Codenamed Cielo, this update will include massive changes, beginning with new features and ending with new app categories finally being unlocked for Android Auto users.
The new update will include support for widgets, something users have been drooling after for several years already. Widgets will be displayed side-by-side with the rest of the Android Auto interface - unlike CarPlay, where widgets are shown on a separate screen - so you will be able to see the weather forecast, the next calendar appointments, and other data directly on the screen, without having to launch the full apps.
Photo: Mishaal Rahman on X The other big feature that will be part of this release is support for video apps. While methods to watch YouTube and play other media from apps not officially available on Android Auto have existed for a long time, Google is now unlocking the support for YouTube and other similar apps officially.
Users will be able to watch YouTube when their cars are stationary directly on their infotainment screens. When they begin driving, and Android Auto detects this, the application restricts the video playback for safety reasons. YouTube will allow an audio-only mode for users who pay for YouTube Premium, so they will be able to continue the playback in the background only by listening to the audio track.
All the other apps that will be able to play video on Android Auto will have to specifically integrate this audio-only mode to be able to continue the playback when the vehicle starts moving.
Browsers will also come to Android Auto. When this feature goes live, users will be able to browse the Internet directly from their infotainment screens, so they won’t need their phones anymore. Obviously, this feature will also be available only when their vehicles are parked, as the browsing won’t be allowed while driving. No further specifics have been shared, but Google Chrome and Vivaldi, the two browsers already available on Android Automotive, are very likely to get support for Android Auto.
Google hasn’t shared any ETA specifics as to when these new features should start rolling out, but there’s a good chance they would start appearing for beta users by the end of the year. Everybody else will get the same capabilities in the first quarter of the next year.
